instruction.text: Listen and select the correct answer.

trainers.hint: This map shows the location of the many hotspots around the world.

atoms.a: Volcanoes can also form at hotspots. What do you think a hotspot is?

b.sound: An area of extreme heat in the Earth’s mantle
An area with extremely cold temperatures

feedback.end: This extreme heat causes the crust directly above the hotspot to melt. This allows magma to burst through, and a volcano forms.

atoms.b: A new chain of islands can be created by a hotspot. This happens when a ((robotic ++tectonic)) plate within the Earth’s ((++crust mantle)) moves over the top of a hotspot.
The heat from the hotspot causes the rock in the Earth’s ((inner_core ++crust)) to melt. Liquid rock rises up through cracks in the surface to form a volcano.
The volcano emerges out of the water above the hotspot, but as the ((mantle ++plate)) travels further away, the volcano becomes extinct, and an island is formed.

instruction.text: Select the highest point on this map.

trainers.hint: This is an elevation map, which shows the changes in the height of land. The lowest areas are shown in green, and the highest are dark brown.

feedback.end: Hawaii is a chain of islands that formed as a result of a hotspot. This chain continues to grow today. The darkest brown area shows the location of the highest point of Hawaii, which is also the current location of the hotspot.

atoms.a: Chains of islands form because of hotspots.
There is a hotspot underneath Hawaii.
Chains of islands form because hotspots move and create a new volcano.

feedback.wrong: Remember, it is the tectonic plate that moves, not the hotspot!
